body: Camel-case is used in SVG so it's not totally unheard of.

I agree that the workarounds are suboptimal and it'd be nice to have a new element (or several) for subheadings. Even my favourite workaround, not included in that article, is suboptimal: ```

Staged proposals at the WHATWG
April 28th, 2025 by Domenic Denicola

``` I would be OK with `` for a subheading under `

`, `` under `

` and so on. For example, instead of: ```

Staged proposals at the WHATWG

April 28th, 2025 by Domenic Denicola
``` we would simply have: ```

Staged proposals at the WHATWG

April 28th, 2025 by Domenic Denicola ``` But I would also suggest an adaptive subheading element such as `` that can be placed inside the heading tag so that it can adapt to any level of heading. For example instead of: ```

Staged proposals at the WHATWG
April 28th, 2025 by Domenic Denicola

``` we could have: ```

Staged proposals at the WHATWG April 28th, 2025 by Domenic Denicola

```

You don't get the automatic styling of the subheading like you do for headings. (The first MDN example is a little misleading because it doesn't show the additional styling needed to get that result.) In fact, I prefer my favourite workaround that I described above (putting `` inside the `` tag), because at least that partially (not completely) solves both of those issues when compared to using `

Perhaps that is where the confusion is arising. > Yeah we don't have that kind of "automatic styling" for subheadings using `

It's the same problem, and it's a problem that many developers have noted and requested a solution to over the years. > What kind of "automatic styling" do you want for subheadings? Any kind using similar design principles to those applied to all of the similar HTML elements like `

`, `

`, `

` etc. Any styling that is appropriate for a subheading, which would make it smaller than the heading that it is placed inside, or that it is placed in the same hgroup as, perhaps proportionate to the size of the associated heading, and otherwise a similar style to the heading to show its relationship to the heading as a subheading. I've shown some examples above, because the workarounds I showed require manual styling, but you can also look at all of the standard subheading styling on blogs etc, that currently are usually done manually, even where the `

`, `

You shouldn't use a HTML element just for its styling, instead you should use it for what semantics it provides. For example, using a `
` to have smaller text shouldn't be done as it affects accessibility. > that is done by design experts and implemented at the browser level. Not really? I'm far from an expert on how difficult it is to add new elements, and whether the difficulty is primarily technical or procedural. I'm only noting that it's not ideal, and I think we can acknowledge an issue regardless of decisions on whether it should currently be a priority to fix it. I'm also still of the opinion that the `` workaround is better, though non-standard and still suboptimal. For what it's worth validator.w3.org finds it to be compliant.
